entities.summary:
Giovanni Maria Vitelleschi (1380–1440) was a prominent Italian cardinal and condottiere who played a pivotal role in the tumultuous politics of Renaissance Italy.

Born into a wealthy mercantile family, Vitelleschi rose through the ranks of the Medici court, eventually becoming a cardinal under Pope Eugenius IV. As a condottiere, he led troops in various battles across Italy, including the infamous siege of Pisa (1400).

Vitelleschi's involvement with the Dominican Order and his appointment as Grand Inquisitor during Pope Martin V's papacy (1417) highlight his complex religious and political allegiances.

Despite his significant influence on Italian politics, Vitelleschi's legacy remains somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries. Nevertheless, he remains an important figure in the annals of Renaissance history, offering valuable insights into the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined this pivotal era.

"The Lord is good, for he has taken away my errors." - Giovanni Maria Vitelleschi
